title: Postcard and Tide
premise: Emrys Reyes, a pastry chef drowning in debt, joins a community pen-pal program meant to pair isolated strangers—only to discover her anonymous correspondent is Theo Vance, the developer whose company is foreclosing on her café and the man she loved and lost a decade ago. Writing under assumed names, they fall for each other a second time while waging open war in daylight: his signature on the demolition order, her flour-dusted defiance. When the truth surfaces, Emrys must finally speak the sentence she has rehearsed for ten years—the reason she left him—and Theo must choose between the empire he built to forget her and the tide that keeps returning them to shore. In the end, he tears up the foreclosure, she says the sentence, and they rebuild the café together on land neither one owns alone.
about_author: Dominic Ishikawa is a former line cook who spent six years writing love letters he never sent from kitchens in Lisbon and Osaka. Postcard and Tide is his second novel, drawn from his belief that every romance is really a negotiation with memory.

chapters.title: Three Missed Payments
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. She counts the café's remaining days in pastry margins and eviction notices, establishing her rule: no love, no risk, no past tense made present. Emotional beat: weary control masking terror.

chapters.title: The Anonymous Assignment
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Her barista Nadia signs them both up for the harbor town's centennial pen-pal project as a morale stunt; Emrys agrees only because the flyer promises anonymity. Beat: reluctant hope.

chapters.title: Dear Stranger
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. He writes his first letter from a glass office above the marina, half-ironic, half-starved, assigned by his own PR team to soften his image. Beat: loneliness beneath power.

chapters.title: Flour and Ink
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Her first letter slips out more honest than intended—she writes about grief without naming it—and she immediately regrets it. Beat: exposure.

chapters.title: The Man at the Counter
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Theo walks into her café to inspect the property before foreclosure; ten years collapse between them. Neither lets the other see it land. Beat: frozen shock.

chapters.title: Enemies, Formally
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. He serves the final notice with corporate courtesy; she throws him out with a tray of burnt madeleines. Both go home shaking. Beat: war declared over an old wound.

chapters.title: What I Didn't Say
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. She drafts a furious letter to her pen-pal about powerful men who take what they want—unknowingly describing Theo to Theo. Beat: catharsis misdirected.

chapters.title: Reading Between Lines
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Her letter's phrasing—a specific childhood detail about gull feathers—snags something in his memory he can't place yet. Beat: first thread of suspicion.

chapters.title: The Rehearsed Sentence
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Flashback chapter: the night she left a decade ago, the sentence she practiced and never delivered, and why she fled this town. Beat: buried grief surfaced.

chapters.title: Zoning Hearing
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. They face each other publicly over the waterfront development; their sparring is so electric the whole room notices. Beat: attraction weaponized.

chapters.title: Letters Get Closer
chapters.summary: Both POVs, interleaved. Their anonymous correspondence turns confessional—he admits he built his empire to stop feeling anything. Beat: intimacy through the veil.

chapters.title: Nadia Knows
chapters.summary: Nadia's POV. She spots Theo rereading a letter in his car outside the café and starts quietly connecting dots. Beat: dramatic irony tightened.

chapters.title: Extension Granted
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Theo unexpectedly grants her café a ninety-day extension, telling himself it's strategy. It isn't. Beat: tenderness disguised as business.

chapters.title: The Tide Pool
chapters.summary: Both POVs. A storm strands them together at the cove where they once were happy; almost-kiss, aborted by a phone call about demolition permits. Beat: longing interrupted.

chapters.title: His Signature
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. She finds Theo's handwriting on the permit file and recognizes it as her pen-pal's hand. She says nothing, testing him. Beat: dread and thrill entwined.

chapters.title: Testing the Water
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. She plants a false secret in her next letter; if it reaches Theo's ears, he is her correspondent. Beat: gambit.

chapters.title: The Trap Springs
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. He references the planted detail in person without thinking; Emrys goes cold mid-service. He realizes too late what he's done. Beat: revelation.

chapters.title: Confrontation at Closing Time
chapters.summary: Both POVs. She confronts him after hours: 'You've been reading my heart to win a lawsuit.' He can't deny it. Beat: betrayal layered over desire.

chapters.title: Silence, Annotated
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. He stops writing; she keeps receiving letters—forged? No: his assistant, covering. The letters turn hollow. Beat: loss of the one honest channel.

chapters.title: The Rival Bidder
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. A second developer offers to save the café—at the price of becoming his showcase girlfriend for press photos. Beat: temptation of the wrong rescue.

chapters.title: Ten Years Ago, Continued
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Deeper flashback: what Theo's family did to hers, the debt that started everything, why the sentence matters. Beat: sympathy rebalanced toward Theo.

chapters.title: He Reads Them All
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Alone in his office, he rereads every letter and understands he has been loved, anonymously, more honestly than ever in his life. Beat: reckoning.

chapters.title: Public Humiliation
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. The rival developer leaks her pen-pal identity to the press to sabotage Theo; the town gossips. Beat: exposure at its cruelest.

chapters.title: Standing in the Doorway
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. He shows up soaked in rain to defend her publicly, then privately begs—not for forgiveness, but for one true conversation. She slams the door. Beat: pride vs. ache.

chapters.title: The Café Fails Anyway
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Despite everything, the bank moves early; equipment auctioned. She bakes one last full menu for the neighborhood. Beat: grief for a dream.

chapters.title: What the Town Remembers
chapters.summary: Nadia's POV. The community rallies—old customers, rivals, even Theo's estranged mother—with stories of Emrys's kindness. Beat: belonging revealed as already present.

chapters.title: The Sentence, Drafted
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. She finally writes the sentence down—the real reason she left—and cannot yet say it aloud. Beat: courage assembling itself.

chapters.title: Boardroom Coup
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. His board, learning of the scandal and his distraction, moves to remove him; the demolition becomes someone else's decision unless he fights. Beat: power turning on its owner.

chapters.title: Last Letter, Unsigned
chapters.summary: Both POVs. Theo sends one final honest letter through the official program—no tricks, no name—confessing everything including the trap he fell into. Beat: naked sincerity.

chapters.title: She Recognizes the Truth
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Reading it at the empty café counter, she weeps into proofing dough and knows the war is over; only the sentence remains. Beat: surrender to feeling.

chapters.title: The Auction Block
chapters.summary: Climax begins. At the property auction, Theo outbids his own company using his personal last assets, then hands the deed to Emrys in front of everyone. Beat: sacrifice made public.

chapters.title: Say It
chapters.summary: Climax. Before the crowd, Emrys finally speaks the rehearsed sentence: 'I left because I was pregnant, and your father paid me to go.' Ten years of silence break. Beat: devastating release.

chapters.title: After the Wave Breaks
chapters.summary: Both POVs. Theo reels—there was a child? No: she lost the pregnancy alone, and hid it to spare him his father's wrath. Grief shared at last. Beat: mourning together.

chapters.title: Rebuilding on Sand
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. They renovate the café side by side, clumsy and tender, learning each other's adult selves. Beat: cautious reconstruction.

chapters.title: His Mother's Visit
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. His mother arrives to apologize for her decade of silence, revealing his father's deathbed regret. Beat: generational wound acknowledged.

chapters.title: First Date, Second Chance
chapters.summary: Both POVs. A proper date at the cove—no letters, no masks, just two people talking badly and laughing well. Beat: joy earned.

chapters.title: Grand Reopening
chapters.summary: Ensemble. The café reopens as 'Postcard & Tide'; the whole town comes; Nadia is made partner. Beat: belonging fulfilled.

chapters.title: The Last Assignment
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. The pen-pal program ends its centennial year; they write one final letter each and read them aloud to each other across a small table. Beat: ritual closure.

chapters.title: Present Tense
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. He proposes not with a ring but with a new lease—one name crossed out, two names written in. She says yes before he finishes. Beat: love in present tense.

chapters.title: Postcard and Tide
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV, epilogue. One year later: morning light, rising bread, a postcard on the counter from a stranger who found hope in their story. She pins it to the wall beside the old eviction notice. Beat: memory honored, future claimed.
